Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

- Key asks from Acme: feature parity with your current hyperscaler endpoints across tool/function calling, structured outputs (schema enforcement + validation), and low-latency streaming. Also concerned about token costs and predictable latency for bursty traffic.
- Redwood differentiators we discussed: runtime-first optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache), streaming with chunked function-call events, and model variant fallbacks for reliability.

Proposed next steps:
1) We attached an initial test plan (acme-eval-test-plan-20260601.xlsx) — covers test vectors for function calling, structured output validation, and streaming latency percentiles. Please confirm or add tests.
2) Our SE (Rishi) will share a short competitive comparison doc (latency vs AWS/Google/Other APIs) and suggested test harness.
3) Run a short synthetic baseline test (we can run from our infra) or, if you prefer, we can run from an Acme account for more realistic network conditions — let us know.
4) Schedule a 30–45 minute results review the week of June 8.

Attachments: acme-eval-test-plan-20260601.xlsx

Thanks — I'll coordinate scheduling once you confirm the tests.

Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and the test plan. A couple clarifying questions from our team before you run anything:

- Streaming: can you share the end-to-end latency we should expect for token-level streaming (50th/95th/99th) for a 1,024 token response when served from us-west region? We care about time-to-first-token and steady-state throughput.
- Tool/function calling: does Redwood support strict JSON schema enforcement on function outputs (i.e., reject non-conformant outputs) or only post-hoc validation? We have workflows that rely on guaranteed structured outputs.
- Cost: rough delta vs our current hyperscaler bill (we use an aggregator of AWS/Anthropic endpoints) — ballpark numbers will help set expectations.

If you can give high-level answers and Rishi can share the comparison doc, we can confirm the tests and preferred run location.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Samantha — quick technical answers below + attaching a short competitive comparison (redwood-vs-hyperscalers-20260602.pdf):

- Streaming latency: typical time-to-first-token from us-west (p95) for a 1k-token generation is ~120–160ms on our hosted endpoints with small-model variants; p99 under steady-state is ~220–350ms depending on quantization/profile and batch mixing. Time-to-first-token can be lower (~80–110ms) for pinned dedicated capacity. We provide token-level SSE streaming; the client receives interleaved function-call events when streaming function calls.

- Tool/function calling: we support both approaches. By default, the model returns candidate structured outputs and we provide a validation layer that can auto-retry or run a strict enforcement mode that rejects non-conformant outputs (and can surface a 400-like error to the client). Enforcement mode has a small latency overhead since we run a lightweight schema validator server-side.

- Structured outputs: we offer schema-aware decoding hooks and a post-generation deterministic canonicalizer to improve parity. For very strict workflows we recommend the enforcement + canonicalizer pipeline in Redwood Optimize.

- Cost: ballpark — our hosted API is often 20–40% lower per-token than top hyperscaler managed endpoints for similar models due to batching and KV cache savings, but exact depends on sequence lengths and cache hit rates. We'll include sample cost comparisons in the attached PDF.

Proposed tests: run the test plan in the attached sheet focusing on three buckets: function-calling (10k calls), structured-output validation (5k samples with varied schemas), and streaming latency (synthetic and real prompts, 1k-token responses). We can run synthetic tests from our infra and share raw metrics; if you want network realism, we can run from an Acme account (we'll need temporary test keys).

Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-20260602.pdf

CC: Marissa & David for scheduling and next steps.

Rishi
